# Sheet — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a sheet when someone needs to work on one thing without losing the place they came from: editing a record's details beside its list, filtering results while keeping them in view. It is modal — the scrim and the focus trap mean the rest of the page waits — so keep the task short and give it a title that says what is being changed. It enters from the right by default; the left is for a document outline or a tree, where the edge matters. If the task belongs to a compact screen or should replace the view rather than accompany it, that is a dialog or a route.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use modal sheets for tasks that need focus — the scrim marks the interruption.
- Let content scroll inside with titles pinned where applicable.

**Don't**

- Don't trap focus without announcing modality.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Container | resting | comp.sheet.container | surface-container-low, 28px leading edge, level3 |
| Scrim | resting | sys.color.scrim | 32% |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| SheetRoot | Owns the open state. Accepts `open`/`onOpenChange` to control it. |
| SheetTrigger | The element that opens the sheet. |
| SheetContent | The panel. Portals to the end of the document, renders the scrim and traps focus. Slides in from `side`. |
| SheetTitle | Names the sheet — what is being worked on. |
| SheetDescription | Supporting line under the title, wired to `aria-describedby`. |
| SheetClose | Closes the sheet from inside it. |
| Sheet | The namespace object: all of the parts above. |

### FAQ

**Bottom drawer or side sheet?**

Bottom drawers rise for compact flows; side sheets dock for persistent panels.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the sheet when a titled surface should come up over what someone is doing and be leavable: a short form, a set of details, a confirmation. It is the plain member of the family — no snap points, no fixed action row, no picker semantics. Visibility is `open` with `onOpenChange` reporting state, like every other sheet in the family and like the dialog.

### Usage

**Do**

- Name the panel with `title` — it is the accessible label.
- Drive `open` from state and mirror `onOpenChange` so dismiss paths (scrim, back, close control) stay in sync.
- Reach for `BottomSheet` or `SnapSheet` when the panel needs snap points or an action row — this one is the plain panel.

**Don't**

- Don't load a full task into a sheet — a route owns long work, a sheet owns a decision.
- Don't hide the only dismissal in a custom child — the close control must stay reachable.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Surface | resting | theme.color.surfaceContainerLow | surfaceContainerLow |
| Dismiss control | resting | theme.color.onSurfaceVariant | onSurfaceVariant, minHeight 48, minWidth 48 |

### FAQ

**`open` or `onDismiss` — which owns the state?**

`open`/`onOpenChange` own the state. `onDismiss` is the dismissal action, fired alongside the `false` report on every dismissal path.

**Sheet, BottomSheet, or SnapSheet?**

Sheet is the plain titled panel. BottomSheet adds the action row; SnapSheet adds snap-point detents. Pick the smallest member that carries the content.
